data.description: I want to experiment with a different player control scheme. Rather than using 4 directional keys we should try Asteroid style controls. That is forward (w or up arrow) and turn left and right (a and s, or left and right arrow). The turn keys will rotate the player. In terms of graphics we will have one thruster opposite to the direction of travel and two smaller (70% size) thrusters on the left and right. The left/right thrusters will be further forward on the ship so that they appear to rotate it. The player gym scene will provide a button to select the control scheme and will provide alternative settings for acceleration, max speed, rotation speed etc. When saving we save the currently chosen control scheme and they settings for that scheme. When implementing this the ships movement controls should be refactored into two pluggable classes. The VFX and SFX should be a part of these classes.
data.title: Alternative player control

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Intake questions for operator:

**Q1: Key mapping**
The description says "turn left and right (a and s, or left and right arrow)." In classic Asteroids, A/Left-arrow = turn left, D/Right-arrow = turn right. Does "a and s" mean A = turn left, S = turn right? Or is S the reverse/backward thrust key?

**Q2: Rotation mechanics**
"Rotation speed" is mentioned as a tunable setting. Should there be a configurable rotationSpeed in the config? Does the ship visually rotate (body + thrusters rotate together) or does the ship face change while thruster positions remain fixed?

**Q3: Pluggable class architecture**
The description says "ships movement controls should be refactored into two pluggable classes." What should these classes represent? E.g., (a) an InputHandler (maps keys to actions) and a MovementModel (applies physics)? Or (b) separate ThrustMovement and AsteroidMovement implementations?
